correctness.rationale: Exact conditional unbiasedness plus a support-closure lemma for division by positive integers proves equality with a single rounding after any finite reciprocal-integer sequence. For nonreciprocal q, an explicit integer initial value gives strictly positive second-step masses at 0,1,2, impossible for a single rounding. The integer quadratic inequality gives universal variance minimality and its strict converse. The two-point marginal laws imply a geometric extinction survival tail and an exact summable mean. The proof checks integer and zero boundaries; packaged Fraction arithmetic corroborates 7100 fixed-step, 208 variable-step, and 130 nonreciprocal rational cases. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

Croci–Giles analyze error bounds; the 2022 survey gives definition and applications; Dahlqvist et al. provide a general distribution-propagation framework, not the asserted closed-form identity. value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of when multi-step unbiased low-precision scalar decay introduces no additional marginal uncertainty beyond one final quantization. Its integer-denominator closure, necessity already at step two, sharp minimal lattice variance, variable-factor commutativity and exact extinction tail address a specific useful numerical-analysis question. The exact q=2/5 example gives a 31/6-fold variance increase, so the boundary separates materially different behavior, not an arbitrary small arithmetic gain. It does not assert operational superiority on IEEE hardware.
